transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, I don't want to make a huge deal out of it, but I've just been having a bit of a hard time lately. 

I just keep feeling like... like I ruined things for everybody? I'm doing my pipefitting apprenticeship right now, and I just feel like a total fake. Like I'm letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices... just over little things, you know? Stuff I know other people would probably just fix and move on from, but I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I'm messing it all up. 

I'm sorry, is it okay to start with that? I just hope I'm explaining it right.
Can you tell me if you've been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy outside of work?

Um, yeah, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really don't want to sound lazy, because I know everyone gets tired after a long shift and it's probably normal to want a break. But... well, lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook without even picking it up. And I've been skipping volleyball, and kind of just... ignoring the group texts from my volunteer group. 

I feel awful even admitting that, because I really hate letting people down or seeming flaky. But I just don't feel much of anything when I look at that stuff right now, even though those used to be the things that made me feel the most like myself. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual even after rest?

Um, I don't think so? I mean, I guess I'm a little tired, but honestly, who isn't, right? It's physical work, so I'm on my feet all day. I really try to get enough sleep so I'm ready for my shift, and I think I'm doing okay with that. I definitely don't want to complain about being tired when I'm just doing my job like everyone else. I'm sorry, is that what you meant? I just don't think my energy is really any different than a normal person working my hours.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, my appetite seems pretty normal to me. I still eat lunch with the crew and make dinner when I get home. I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything like that. 

I really try to make sure I'm eating enough so I have the strength for work, you know? I wouldn't want to fall behind just because I wasn't taking care of myself. So, yeah, I think my eating habits are totally fine. I hope that's okay? I just haven't really noticed any big changes there.
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed or down that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Um... oh, gosh. That's a really heavy question. I... I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or unstable or anything, because I'm not. I promise I would never actually do anything to hurt myself. I don't have a plan or anything scary like that. 

But... well, sometimes, like when I'm driving home after class, or when I'm just lying awake at night... I do get these thoughts. Just... passing thoughts, really. Like maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up tomorrow. 

I know that sounds bad, and I'm really sorry if that's alarming. I try to push those thoughts away as soon as they happen because I know I have responsibilities and people who count on me. It's just... sometimes it feels like a lot. Is it... is it somewhat normal to feel that way when you're just really overwhelmed? I hope I'm not making things sound worse than they are.
Have you found that things that used to bring you joy, like your sketchbook or volleyball, don’t feel enjoyable at all anymore, even a little bit?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm totally checked out or anything, because I'm definitely still trying to keep up with everything. I know how important it is to stay active.

But... yeah, lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook, and I've been skipping volleyball practice. Even the volunteer group texts, I just kind of ignore them, and I don't really feel much of anything about it. Which is weird, because those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? 

I'm probably just letting the stress get to me a bit too much, right? I really am trying to get back into it. I just... I hope it's okay that I haven't been as involved lately. It's just a phase, I'm sure. Is that something that happens when you're just working a lot?
How long have you been feeling this way? When did these feelings start, or when did you first notice them?

Um... well, it's been a little while, I guess. I really hope I haven't been letting it affect my work for too long, because I really pride myself on being reliable. 

But, um, I suppose this... this depressed stretch, or whatever you want to call it... it's been with me for about nine months now? I was trying really hard to just push through it and not make a big deal out of it. I didn't want anyone to think I couldn't handle my responsibilities. 

It just... it became a lot harder to hide once my schoolwork and my job started slipping a bit. I'm really sorry if that sounds like I've been irresponsible. I promise I've been trying my best to keep everything together. Is it... is it normal for it to last that long without getting better on its own? I really hope I'm not doing something wrong to make it stick around.
Can you tell me if you’ve felt like you can’t enjoy anything at all lately, even things you used to really like doing?

Um, yeah... I think we might have just touched on that a second ago, actually. I'm really sorry if I wasn't clear enough before, I hope I'm answering your questions right. 

But, um, yes... like I was saying, it's just... lately I can walk right past my sketchbook, or skip my volleyball games, and I just kind of ignore the group texts for my volunteer stuff. And I really don't feel much of anything about it, which is the weird part. Those used to be the things that made me feel like, well, me. 

I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing absolutely nothing, though! I'm still trying to be productive. It's just... the enjoyment part is kind of missing right now. I'm sure I just need to try a little harder to get engaged again, right? I really want to be back to my normal self.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down, or that you're moving more slowly than usual, like you're in a fog or under water?

Um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want it to sound like I'm slacking off at work or anything, because I really do try to keep up my pace. Being a pipefitter is hard work, and I know my crew relies on me. 

But... yeah, I suppose lately on the job, I'll catch myself just moving a bit slow. Like, it takes this extra effort just to climb down into a trench for a fitting, or even just to answer the foreman when he asks me a question. My brain just feels a little... fuzzy, maybe? 

A couple of the guys have even asked if I'm sick or hungover, which is really embarrassing because I'm definitely not! I'm just... I don't know, maybe just a little worn out? I'm really trying to snap out of it so I don't slow the team down. Do you think that's just from being tired, or is that part of all this too? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Can you tell me if you've been feeling unusually fatigued or run down, even when you're not at work or right after a day off?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely get tired, but I think that's just normal, right? My job is pretty physical, so it makes sense that I'd be a little wiped out at the end of the day. 

I really try to make the most of my days off, though! I don't want to just lay around all weekend, so I try to stay busy. I mean, maybe I'm a little less energetic than usual, but I don't think it's anything extreme. I'm definitely not sleeping the day away or anything like that. I always make sure I'm up and ready to go if someone needs me. 

Is it okay if I'm just a normal amount of tired? I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you found that you don’t get any pleasure or interest out of almost all activities lately, even the ones you usually enjoy?

Um, yeah, I think we... we actually just talked about that a little bit, didn't we? I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself or if I didn't explain it right the first time. I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. 

But yes, like I mentioned, it's just... I can walk right past my sketchbook these days, or skip my volleyball games, and I'll see the group texts for my volunteer stuff and just ignore them. And I don't really feel anything about it, which is the part that worries me. Those were always the things that made me feel like me, you know? 

I'm really trying not to let it get me down, though. I know I just need to push myself a little harder to get back into it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Have you felt that nothing, even things you used to enjoy, gives you any sense of pleasure or interest, almost all the time lately?

Um, yeah, I... I think we might have just covered that, actually? I'm really sorry if I wasn't clear before, I know I'm probably not the best at explaining all this. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.

But yeah, it's just like I was saying... I'll walk right past my sketchbook, or I'll skip my volleyball games, and I'll see the group texts for my volunteer stuff and just... ignore them. And I don't really feel much of anything about it, which is the part that kind of scares me, because those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? 

I really don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or giving up on things. I'm honestly trying to stay positive and push through it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm doing this right.
Can you tell me if you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to care about, like your sketchbook or spending time with friends, almost every day for the past several weeks?

Oh, um... wow, I'm so sorry, I feel like I keep repeating the same thing to you. I must be doing a really bad job of explaining myself, and I really don't want to waste your time. 

But yes, it's... it's exactly like you said. And like I was trying to say before. I just... I don't really care about my sketchbook right now, or volleyball, or the volunteer stuff. It's been like that for a few weeks, I guess. I just walk by it all and feel... nothing. 

I'm really trying to get my spark back, though! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around wallowing or anything. I'm sure it's just a phase and I'll snap out of it soon. I'm really trying my best to be a good patient for you, I promise. Does that answer what you were looking for?
Can you tell me if you've felt like nothing, absolutely nothing, gives you any sense of pleasure or interest, almost every day for the past two weeks?

Oh my gosh... I am so, so sorry. I feel terrible. I must be doing a really awful job of explaining this if you have to keep asking me the same thing. I'm really not trying to be difficult or waste your time, I promise! 

But, um, yes... for the past couple of weeks, it's exactly what we were just talking about. I'll just completely ignore my sketchbook, or I'll skip my volleyball games, and I won't even look at the group texts for my volunteer work. And I just don't feel much of anything at all about it, even though those are the main things that usually make me feel like myself. 

I'm really trying to push past it and stay positive, though! I swear I'm not just giving up or being lazy. Did... did I finally answer that the way you needed me to? I really, really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down, or that you're moving more slowly than usual, like you're in a fog or under water?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really hope it's not affecting my work too much, I always try to be a good worker. But, um... yeah, on the job lately, I've caught myself just moving a bit slow. 

Like, it feels like it takes extra effort just to climb down into a trench for a fitting, or... or even just to answer the foreman when he asks me a question. My brain just feels a little foggy, I suppose. A couple of the guys actually asked if I was sick or hungover, which was super embarrassing because I'm really not! I promise I'm not showing up to work hungover or anything like that. 

I think I'm just a little run down right now, you know? I'm sure I'll be back up to speed in no time. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
